courses.name: Freshman Seminar for Computing
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Introduces new Bellini College students to degree choices, academic requirements and support resources.

category_review.rationale: The entire description is first-year orientation and academic navigation; it does not establish programming or other computing subject content.

courses.name: Programming Concepts
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Introduces programming concepts and design methods through a contemporary programming language.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: ACT Math (min score 24) OR College Algebra MPT (min score 12) OR College-Level Math CPT (min score 60) OR SAT Math (min score 570); Course restrictions: Majors Only

category_review.rationale: The description expressly centers programming and software design.

courses.name: Composition I
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Introduces rhetorical analysis, audience-aware writing, composition processes and language conventions.
courses.prerequisites: Other information: Scores of: STI1 of 440 or TFL4 of 550 or TFIT of 079 or EAC1 of 17 or EAC3 of 18.

category_review.rationale: Rhetoric and written communication are the explicit subjects.

courses.name: Calculus I
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Studies single-variable limits, derivatives and integrals, with optimization and other applications.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: MAC 1147 (min grade C) OR SAT Math (min score 670) OR ACT Math (min score 29) OR College-Level Math CPT (min score 90) OR PreCalc & Trig MPT (min score 12); Other information: Knowledge of trigonometry.

category_review.rationale: Calculus concepts and mathematical problem solving are explicit.

courses.name: Program Design
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Develops program design and construction using C in a networked environment.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: COP 2510 (min grade B) AND MAC 2311 (min grade B); Course restrictions: Consent of Instructor or Department,Majors Only,Permit Required

category_review.rationale: Program construction is the central subject; a networked setting does not make this a networking-infrastructure course.

courses.name: Composition II
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Practices effective reading, writing and public speaking.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: ENC 1101 (min grade C-)

category_review.rationale: The description centers human communication.

courses.name: Calculus II
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Develops integration, series and elementary transcendental functions for mathematical problem solving.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: MAC 2311 OR MAC 2281 (min grade C); Other information: No credit for students with credit in MAC 2242 or MAC 2282.

category_review.rationale: The description centers calculus and mathematical methods.

courses.name: General Physics I - Calculus Based
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Introduces calculus-based mechanics, fluids, oscillations and waves for science and engineering students.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: MAC 2281 OR MAC 2311 (both min grade C-); Co-prerequisites: PHY 2048L (min grade C-); Other information: Must be taken concurrently with lab and, if dropped, then dropped simultaneously. May not receive credit for both the PHY 2053 and PHY 2048 courses. Not repeatable.

category_review.rationale: Physics is substantive domain knowledge; using calculus does not make the course mathematical theory or computing foundations.

courses.name: General Physics I Laboratory
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Provides the first laboratory in the two-semester general-physics sequence for physics and engineering students.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: MAC 2281 OR MAC 2311 (both min grade C-); Co-prerequisites: PHY 2048 (min grade C-); Other information: Must be taken concurrently with lecture and, if dropped, then dropped simultaneously. May not receive credit for both the PHY 2053L and PHY 2048L courses.

category_review.rationale: Experimental physics is the stated domain practice; the whole sequence topic list is not a claim that this laboratory alone covers every listed topic.

courses.name: Computer Organization
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Introduces digital hardware, processor organization, memory and I/O, with computer arithmetic and assembly programming.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: COP 2510 (min grade B) AND PHY 2048 (min grade B); Course restrictions: Consent of Instructor or Department,Majors Only

category_review.rationale: Computer architecture and hardware organization dominate the description.

courses.name: Introduction to Discrete Structures
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Introduces sets, propositional logic and finite algebraic structures with computing applications.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: MAC 2311 (min grade C)

category_review.rationale: The actual description centers mathematical structures and logic, rather than implementing data structures or algorithms.

courses.name: Data Structures
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Studies and implements data structures for clear, efficient programs, including functional-programming concepts.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: COP 3514 (min grade B) AND CDA 3103 (min grade B) AND COT 3100 (min grade B); Course restrictions: Majors Only

category_review.rationale: The description centers data structures, representations and programming.

courses.name: Introduction to Linear Systems
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Studies matrix algebra, differential equations and finite differences.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: (MAC 2282 (min grade C) AND MAC 2312 (min grade C)) OR AP Calculus BC (min score 4)

category_review.rationale: The description is mathematical methods; the title does not establish computing systems.

courses.name: Introduction to Psychological Science
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Introduces scientific study of human behavior and mental processes through historical and current psychological perspectives.

category_review.rationale: The description centers human behavior and cognition; it does not state an AI methods curriculum.

courses.name: Analysis of Algorithms
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Studies design principles and analytical techniques for commonly used computer algorithms.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: COP 4530

category_review.rationale: Algorithm design and analysis are explicit computing foundations.

courses.name: Natural Language Processing
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Introduces computational natural-language processing through linguistic phenomena, formal methods and applications.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: COP 4530 (min grade C); Course restrictions: Majors Only

category_review.rationale: Natural-language processing is an explicitly described AI-focused subfield.

courses.name: Probability and Statistics with Calculus
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Introduces probability and statistical analysis, with critical data interpretation and problem solving.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: [MAC 2282 (min grade C) OR MAC 2312 (min grade C)] OR AP Calculus BC (min score 4)

category_review.rationale: Probability and statistical methods are the named subject, independent of the engineering prefix.

courses.name: Introductory Statistics I
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Applies descriptive and inferential statistics to data interpretation and contextual problems.

category_review.rationale: Statistical methods are explicit; application across disciplines does not change the primary subject.

courses.name: American National Government
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Studies U.S. constitutional government, its historical foundations, institutions, policies and citizen participation.

category_review.rationale: Political institutions and civic participation are the primary subject.

courses.name: American History I
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Examines U.S. history before European contact through Reconstruction, including constitutional development, slavery and the Civil War.

category_review.rationale: The description explicitly studies social and political history.

courses.name: American History II
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Traces U.S. history after Reconstruction through the contemporary era, including industrialization, war, constitutional change and civil rights.

category_review.rationale: The description explicitly studies social and political history.

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence Fundamentals
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Introduces AI vocabulary, capabilities, limitations and applications in nontechnical terms.

category_review.rationale: The actual description introduces AI concepts and capabilities.

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence Applications
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Builds AI applications with low-code or no-code tools, language-model workflows, retrieval and agents; team projects evaluate performance, cost and responsible use.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: [COP 2510 (min grade B) OR CGS 2060 (min grade B)] AND CAI 1000 (min grade B)

category_review.rationale: The description teaches language-model workflows, retrieval augmentation and agents.

courses.name: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Introduces AI methods and software for search, reasoning and learning, including basic machine learning.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: COP 3514 (min grade B) AND CDA 3103 (min grade B); Co-prerequisites: COP 4530; Course restrictions: Majors Only

category_review.rationale: Search, reasoning and learning techniques are explicitly central.

courses.name: Ethical Issues in Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Examines professional and ethical responsibilities in AI through developing and presenting responses to real-world problems.

category_review.rationale: Professional ethics and responsibilities are the stated subject.

courses.name: Introduction to Machine Learning
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Surveys supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement and deep learning, emphasizing evaluation and responsible practice.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: CAI 4002 (min grade C)

category_review.rationale: Supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning methods are primary.

courses.name: Deep Learning
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Covers neural-network mathematics, single- and multilayer models, applications and ethical concerns.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: COP 4530 (min grade C)

category_review.rationale: Neural-network learning methods are explicitly primary.

courses.name: AI System Architecture and Infrastructure
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Studies AI training/deployment infrastructure, frameworks, data pipelines, distributed systems and cloud scaling through practical system design.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: CDA 3103 (min grade B) AND CAI 4002 (min grade C)

category_review.rationale: The stated focus is infrastructure, deployment, distributed systems and cloud scaling.

courses.name: Computer Vision
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Introduces image formation and segmentation, feature matching, shape and texture analysis, object recognition and changing scenes.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: COP 4530 (min grade C)

category_review.rationale: Image interpretation, visual recognition and scene analysis establish computer vision.

requirements.title: General education and unrestricted electives
requirements.summary: Brochure lists state natural science and humanities, USF humanities and social sciences, and unrestricted electives. Approved pools and overlap rules remain unreviewed.

requirements.title: Advising and optional experiences
requirements.summary: Sequence is recommended for full-time students. Students not calculus-ready can start with precalculus with advising. Summer research, abroad and internship experiences are recommendations, not mandatory courses.

requirements.title: University minimum degree credits
requirements.summary: Registrar overview gives 120 credit hours for this university requirement; program-specific requirements may be stricter. The normalized unit and detailed applicability remain unverified.

requirements.title: University minimum upper-level credits
requirements.summary: Registrar overview gives 42 credit hours for this university requirement; program-specific requirements may be stricter. The normalized unit and detailed applicability remain unverified.

requirements.title: Published summer-enrollment minimum
requirements.summary: Registrar overview gives 9 credit hours for this university requirement; program-specific requirements may be stricter. The normalized unit and detailed applicability remain unverified. The registrar FAQ permits documented waiver requests; entry-cohort exceptions remain unresolved.

requirements.title: University final-credit residency
requirements.summary: Complete 30 of the final 60 credit hours at USF according to the registrar overview. Additional major/college residency requirements remain unverified.

requirements.title: Conditional summer-enrollment waiver
requirements.summary: A waiver may be requested for documented seasonal summer employment in each summer missed, unavailable program courses certified by an advisor, or exceptional hardship outside the student’s control. Submit supporting evidence during the graduation-application semester; allow three weeks for a decision. A request is not automatic approval.

requirements.title: Grade-forgiveness limits
requirements.summary: Both attempts must be at USF; the repeat grade must be at least D. At most three forgiveness uses are allowed, with one repeat per course. Academic-dishonesty FF grades are excluded, and forgiveness cannot change courses counted toward an already awarded bachelor’s degree. This does not establish AI-major passing grades.

requirements.title: General education: 36 published credit hours
requirements.summary: Complete 15 state-core and 21 USF-designated credit hours across five disciplines, including the additional two-course choice below. Current approved course attributes determine eligibility; no finite pool is inferred.

requirements.title: Communication
requirements.summary: Three state-core credits plus three USF-designated credits in this discipline; choose currently approved courses. Credit unit normalization remains unverified.

requirements.title: Humanities
requirements.summary: Three state-core credits plus three USF-designated credits in this discipline; choose currently approved courses. Credit unit normalization remains unverified.

requirements.title: Mathematics
requirements.summary: Three state-core credits plus three USF-designated credits in this discipline; choose currently approved courses. Credit unit normalization remains unverified.

requirements.title: Natural Science
requirements.summary: Three state-core credits plus three USF-designated credits in this discipline; choose currently approved courses. Credit unit normalization remains unverified.

requirements.title: Social Science
requirements.summary: Three state-core credits plus three USF-designated credits in this discipline; choose currently approved courses. Credit unit normalization remains unverified.

requirements.title: Two further general-education courses
requirements.summary: Choose two courses totaling six published credits from any of the five general-education disciplines.

requirements.title: Enhancement and state-core reuse rules
requirements.summary: Enhancement labels impose no separate student quota. A state-core course may sometimes serve as a general-education elective; an advisor must confirm the major-specific use. This does not authorize double-counting one course in two slots.

requirements.title: Current course-attribute approval
requirements.summary: Use the public Course Inventory and filter Course Attributes by the required general-education discipline. Approval is a current designation; the full changing pool is not invented from brochure examples.

requirements.title: Civic-literacy entry cohorts
requirements.summary: Complete applicable civic literacy before graduation. The entry date at a Florida public institution controls: before Summer B 2018 generally exempt; Summer B 2018–Summer A 2021 requires course or assessment; Summer B 2021 onward requires both. Out-of-state and additional-degree students are not categorically exempt; the FAQ requires returning earlier graduates to fulfill previously unmet civic literacy.

requirements.title: Approved course and assessment routes
requirements.summary: Course options are POS 2041, AMH 2020, AMH 2010 completed Fall 2024 onward, or transfer-only AMS X010 from Fall 2024 onward. Assessment uses FCLE or approved acceleration. The internal USF Canvas test is available only to pre-Fall-2024 entrants and requires 60%, with unlimited attempts.

requirements.title: Civic transfer and prior assessment evidence
requirements.summary: Florida public-college/university credit needs official transcript evidence for each completed component; an incomplete component remains due. A high-school FCLE pass of at least 60% needs the official transcript and satisfies assessment only. Out-of-state course substitutions require an advisor-submitted syllabus review.

requirements.title: General-education overlap and passing grade
requirements.summary: POS X041, AMH X010 and AMH X020 may also meet state-core social science with C− or better. A lower passing grade may satisfy civic literacy alone. AMH X010 must be completed Fall 2024 onward. Naturalization testing does not satisfy the assessment.

requirements.title: Approved acceleration mechanisms
requirements.summary: Both components: AP US Government ≥3, AP US History ≥4, CLEP American Government ≥50, or CLEP US History I ≥50. Course only: AICE US History A-level A–E, CLEP US History II ≥50, IB History of the Americas 5–7, or passing approved dual enrollment (Fall 2024 timing applies to AMH X010/AMS X010).

requirements.title: Statewide course-equivalency framework
requirements.summary: SCNS equivalence ordinarily requires the same prefix/last three digits, comparable faculty credentials and the applicable minimum grade; equivalent transferred work serves requirements on the same basis as native credit. Quarter and semester amounts may differ. Other credit acceptance remains institution-specific.

requirements.title: Exceptions to automatic course equivalency
requirements.summary: Individual review applies to unoffered or unaccredited/pre-transfer-date courses; 900–999 special work; adult applied academics; graduate courses; internships, apprenticeships, practica, clinical or abroad experiences; and performing-art/Criminal Justice skill courses. These exceptions do not establish approval for an AI requirement.
